It is interesting that the headline in GPT 5.5 launch is not just what the model can do, but how many tokens it takes to do it. For a while, model capability mostly meant: can the model handle the task at all? Progress looked like bigger models, bigger context windows, more tokens, and more compute. That made sense when the main problem was simply getting useful output in the first place. But once models become broadly useful, the evaluation changes. Cost and latency stop being secondary concerns and start becoming part of the capability signal. A model that gets to the right answer in 500 tokens is meaningfully better than one that circles for 5,000 tokens before landing in the same place. The final answer may be similar, but the path matters. At scale, that path shows up in cost, latency, reliability, throughput, and user experience. So the better question is no longer: did the model get the task right? It is becoming more and more: how cleanly did it get the task right under a fixed budget of tokens, time, and context? That is one way to read “gets what to do” points to. The model reads the task correctly, uses the right tool, uses the right context, ignores what does not matter, and avoids unnecessary rambling. Part of this is the model itself becoming sharper. But part of it is also the system around the model: better harnesses, better context management, and better taste about what to include or ignore. This is why accuracy, cost, and latency should be evaluated and measured together as a combined measure of capability. The next important metric is going to be capability per token: how much useful work a model can do for a given budget of context, cost and time. The new and upcoming wave of models, benchmarks and architectures will be judged this way. It's going to be better outcomes with fewer wasted tokens, for everyone. At Mem0 , this is how we already think about memory systems and benchmarks. Our new algorithm is a step toward making capability per token a standard way to evaluate memory in production.

Our latest In Context newsletter breaks down BEAM, the memory benchmark that tests AI agents at up to 10M tokens, based on “Beyond a Million Tokens: Benchmarking and Enhancing Long-Term Memory in LLMs” (ICLR 2026). Full breakdown ↓

We recently released a token-efficient memory algorithm for agents at Mem0 . Our latest memory system achieves 91.6 on LoCoMo, 93.4 on LongMemEval, and 64.1 / 48.6 on BEAM (1M / 10M), while averaging < 7,000 tokens per retrieval call, at 3–4x lower token cost. Typically, full-context approaches on these benchmarks typically run at 25,000+ tokens. What this means for developers: you can run agent memory that is cost-efficient at production scale without sacrificing quality. The goal was to make memory work under real-world constraints, limited context windows, latency budgets, and production scale. What changed: - Single-pass, add-only extraction (~50% faster) - Agent-generated facts treated as first-class - Entity linking across people, places, and concepts - Multi-signal retrieval (semantic + keyword + entity) - Keyword normalization for better recall Full evaluation framework is open source. Available today on our platform and open-source SDK https://mem0.ai/research

Introducing Mem0 CLI A way to give your agents memory directly from the terminal. As agents become more capable, one thing is still missing: they don’t remember. At Mem0 , we believe memory is the missing layer for stateful AI systems. That’s why we built mem0 CLI, you can: - Add, search, and retrieve memory - Store preferences across agents and users - Persist context beyond a single session - Work with structured, schema-driven (JSON) memory Just plug it in, and your agents start remembering. This is designed for both: - Developers building agent workflows - Agents that need to manage their own memory We’re excited about what this unlocks: more personalized, context-aware, and stateful AI systems. Get started: npm install -g @mem0/cli Open source ↓

Yesterday, We took over NVIDIA GTC. We showed up with 5,000 cold water bottles and people in Mem0 swag at every corner. NVIDIA GTC is the Super Bowl of AI conferences. Which means there is AI branding everywhere. From banners, to wrapped cyber trucks and digital billboard trucks. Very quickly, 450+ logos become a blur. So instead of paying $50,000 for a sponsorship seat and just another branded taxi, we showed up IRL. Real people, real conversations, real laughs, and something that people needed: Cold water in 90° weather and some Jensen Huang slander on a t-shirt. The reactions: "Mem0 is literally everywhere." "You guys are doing God's work with this water." "The t-shirts are hilarious." Plus a ton of demos booked. Memory in an AI agent solves personalization, and nothing demonstrates personalization better than actually showing up in person. We remembered what you forget in a hot days. If you're building AI agents and are curious about memory, book a free consultation call here: https://dub.sh/GE0txVo

Most teams treat open source as a distribution strategy. That’s the wrong frame. We build Mem0 Alerts Service in the open because it makes the product better. Contributors catch things we miss. Iterations happen faster. The feedback loop is tighter. I’ve spent most of my career in open source and have seen that shared ownership accelerates everything. That’s what you’re seeing in the weekly updates. We’re hiring engineers who want to build this way. If that’s you, let’s talk.

Amorphic Labs (YC S26) is building AI agents that help sales teams create personalized product demo videos at scale. Sales teams don’t have time to create personalized demos for every prospect they reach out to, even when those demos would be valuable, and they spend hours every week recording demos for post-call follow-ups and inbound requests. Agents that create personalized demo videos solve both problems, making it possible to give every prospect a tailored experience throughout the sales process while saving sales reps hours of time. Getting started is simple: provide a demo account and a list of prospects. The agent researches each prospect, seeds personalized data in your app, uses your software on its own computer like a real sales engineer, and records a workflow tailored to each prospect. It then edits and narrates the video so it is ready to send as a link. Sales teams can show every prospect exactly how their product addresses their specific pain points without spending additional time recording. Founders Dylan Kelly and Frank Li have been friends for close to a decade. Dylan was a quantitative trading intern at UBS and a World Schools Debating Championship finalist. Frank was a Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI and previously interned at Two Sigma, NVIDIA, and Amazon. They were frustrated by how time-consuming it was to create personalized product demos and decided to solve that problem for sales teams. Learn more at amorphiclabs.com or email founders@amorphiclabs.com . Congrats on the launch, Dylan and Frank! 🚀 https://lnkd.in/gAKzkfhJ

Excited to launch Primitive Labs! Our mission is to make human behavior a first-class primitive of software development. We are happy to announce that we are backed by a16z speedrun, with participation from Olive Tree Capital, Unexpected Investments, and Cloverfield Fund. Also, Primitive Labs will be participating in the upcoming a16z SR007 cohort beginning in July! Jean , Gabriel , and I were all shaped by the same lesson that great products begin with the customer. In meeting rooms, an empty chair represented the customer. It was a reminder that every important product decision should begin with the people the product is built for. As AI changes how software is built, customer understanding is becoming the defining constraint in product development. Even further, as software begins to build itself, knowing what to build becomes the bottleneck. Generic intelligence designs for averages. Real users are not averages. Primitive Labs is building behavioral intelligence for AI-native software. Excited to share more in the coming weeks as we continue building with our early design partners. If interested in partnering, please sign up on the waitlist at our website! This company wouldn't exist without an incredible group of investors, advisors, and angels. Everyone says AI is going to kill SaaS. We're betting it rebuilds it. Today we're announcing Ergo 's $2.8M seed, led by FundersClub . We now manage over $3B in pipeline for revenue teams. With participation from Y Combinator , Georgia Institute of Technology , Coughdrop Capital , Kulveer Taggar , and many more. Every revenue team runs on conversations: cold calls, meetings, emails, Slack threads, in person meetings, and more. That's where the real signal lives, and today it's scattered across a dozen tools, and most of it goes nowhere. Ergo is the revenue infrastructure layer for AI-native GTM teams. We capture every conversation, turn it into a unified data layer, and run agents on top for follow-ups, CRM automations, coaching, forecasting, reporting — so reps spend less time on manual admin, no deals slip through the cracks, and leaders get a pipeline they can actually trust. Teams like Rho , Corgi , Retell , Agency Cybersecurity , Greptile , Sully.ai , and more already run on Ergo . The next generation of GTM won't be built on software designed for humans doing manual entry. It'll be built on infrastructure designed for agents and humans to move forward together. Thank you to our investors, customers, and the team who got us here. We're just getting started, and did a full brand refresh. Come see what Ergo can do, website linked in the comment section!
